TV Time shut down last month, and now one of the app's co-founders, Antonio Pinto, has announced a new TV and film tracking app called Bingers that leans further into the social side. Here's what you need to know.

Bingers is now available to download

When Whip Media announced it was shutting down TV Time, one of its co-founders immediately unveiled Bingers, billing it as a "fast, beautiful watchlist with a fun community."

Now, per TechCrunch, Bingers is available to download on iOS and Android, offering some sense of spiritual continuation for users who hadn't yet found a replacement. TV Time was once one of the most widely-used TV and film tracking apps worldwide.

Old users who saved their data via TV Time's export tool can import their archives into Bingers and pick up right where they left off, while those who never exported — or newcomers to TV and film tracking apps — can simply start fresh.

Bingers leans heavily into community-driven features, including user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIFs, polls, and character popularity votes. Pinto told TechCrunch that these were exactly the features that kept users coming back to TV Time:

For those who simply want to keep track of what they've watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlists and viewing history. Like TV Time, it also includes a calendar showing upcoming episodes and premiere dates, along with countdowns to when new content drops.

Bingers is available as a free download on the App Store, and currently has no in-app purchases.
